overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law because the April 30 notice's '208 Update' and 'RPP Update' topics were too vague for the public, while the other topics were adequate; it ordered future compliance and warned that repeat violations may be treated as intentional.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the April 30 notice was not specific enough; the '208 Update' and 'RPP Update' topics used unexplained acronyms and gave lay readers too little detail.
allegations.key_passage: they did not provide enough detail so that a member of the general public without specialized knowledge of the business of the Committee could read the notice and understand the anticipated nature of the discussion.

allegations.summary: Complaint covered the rest of the April 30 notice, including Chairman/Executive Director Activities Update, adoption of minutes, and Other Business; the AG reviewed them as well.
allegations.key_passage: the remaining topics on the meeting notice at issue were sufficiently specific to comply with the law's requirements

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Committee that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
